lines: Finding the right work is harder when everyone asks if you found it yet.
Work is work. Finding the right work is the tricky part.
Waiting for work is still work if you look <pulse>worried enough</pulse>.
Where do I fit? Somewhere useful, I hope, preferably before supper.
People with trades get tasks. People without trades get errands.
A fair chance is easier to ask for than to recognize.
I am trying to look useful, not involved.
Keep your voice even. I am measuring more than your words.
Some questions are safer when they stand a little farther away.
I followed you once and learned something: I need better shoes before I choose a trade.
I remember following you through that road. My feet remember it even better.
That trip across that road taught me to ask more questions before walking.
I followed you into a boat once. Not a trade, apparently, but it felt like training.
That boat trip still sits oddly in my memory, but at least it floated.
A boat can make a bad plan quieter. It cannot make me forget it.
